label: rem:up-quark-properties
title: Up quark: crossing orientation and isolation
html:
Crossing orientation. Within \mathcal{B}_3, each component passes over and under the other two at specific crossings. The positive orientation means the up quark's crossings contribute +q to the Skein polynomial at each crossing point.

What the orientation fixes, and what it does not. The Coulomb charge Q = \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-) is odd under reversal of every crossing. Orientation therefore fixes the sign of the up quark's charge, and fixes its magnitude relative to the down quark — the two are exact mirrors, so their charges are equal and opposite. It does not fix the value +\tfrac{2}{3}, for two independent reasons: a mirror pair has ratio -1, whereas (+\tfrac{2}{3}, -\tfrac{1}{3}) has ratio -2; and Q takes values in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}, so thirds lie outside its range for every braid word. The Standard Model values are adopted here, not derived from the crossing count. The parameter-free ribbon route to them is recorded as tested and refuted in the flavor charge assignments.

Isolation. An isolated up quark does not exist. Removing it from \mathcal{B}_3 unlinks the remaining two unknots, which destroys the baryon.
